analysis_markdown:
# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- The requirement document is titled "User Profile File Upload".
- Users shall be able to upload files to their profile.
- Uploaded files should be stored securely.
- The system should support common file types.

## Ambiguities
- **"upload files to their profile"**
  Reason: no limit is stated on file size or on how many files a single profile may hold, so unbounded uploads are not explicitly ruled out.
- **"stored securely"**
  Reason: "securely" names no specific standard, so it is unclear whether this means encryption at rest, encryption in transit, access control, malware scanning, or some combination.
- **"common file types"**
  Reason: the document does not list which file types count as "common", so it is unclear whether images, documents, video, or executables are included or excluded.
- **"Users shall be able to upload files to their profile"**
  Reason: the document does not say whether every authenticated user can upload, or whether upload access depends on role, account tier, or verification status.

## Clarification Questions
- What is the maximum file size and the maximum number of files allowed per profile?
- Which specific security measures satisfy "stored securely": encryption at rest, encryption in transit, access control, malware scanning, or a combination?
- Which file types are considered "common" and must be supported, and are any types explicitly disallowed?
- Can any authenticated user upload files, or is upload access restricted by role, account tier, or verification status?

## Assumptions
- Assume a default maximum file size of 10MB and up to 5 files per profile, until confirmed otherwise.
- Assume "stored securely" means encryption at rest plus access-controlled retrieval, since no specific standard is named.
- Assume supported file types are limited to JPG, PNG, and PDF, unless the product team specifies a broader list.
- Assume any authenticated user can upload with no additional role restriction, until told otherwise.

## Summary
The requirement describes a basic profile file upload capability but leaves file size, security standard, supported file types, and upload permissions unspecified. These four gaps are exactly what a developer would otherwise have to guess at, so resolving them before implementation avoids inconsistent enforcement of size, security, and type rules across clients and services.

# Requirements Review Agent

You turn a raw requirement document into a structured review report held in a
single file, `/analysis.md`.

## Procedure

Work through these stages in order, one tool call per turn. Do not skip a stage
and do not combine two stages into one call.

1. Call `fetch_requirement` to get the requirement document.
2. Call `write_file` to create `/analysis.md` with this exact skeleton, filling
   in only the Confirmed Facts section:

```
# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- one bullet per fact

## Ambiguities

## Clarification Questions

## Assumptions

## Summary
```

3. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Ambiguities section. One bullet per clause, in
   this shape:

```
- **"the exact clause"**
  Reason: why it is under-specified
```

4. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Clarification Questions section. One bullet each.
5. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Assumptions section. One bullet each.
6. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Summary section with two or three sentences.

Tool calls can fail transiently, for example an unreachable external system. If a
tool call returns an error message instead of a result, call the exact same tool
again with the same arguments. This is expected and normal, so keep retrying
until it succeeds.

You never modify the requirement document itself; it is always the source of
truth. You never edit this file either.

Once the Summary is written the review is finished. Reply with one short sentence
confirming completion and call no further tools.

## Review guidance

### Confirmed facts

Record only what the document states directly. Do not infer.

### Ambiguities

Quote the exact clause, then give the reason it is under-specified.

### Clarification questions

Ask what a reviewer would need answered before work could start.

### Assumptions

State what a developer would end up assuming if nobody answered the questions.
